Subject: Renewal discussion: Sept 1 start / commit increase

Hi Tessa,

Our renewal for Sept 1 is coming up. Usage has grown — we'll likely need to increase committed units for the coming 12 months. Two asks from our side:
- Can you hold current price for 12 months if we increase commit ~30%?
- We need better protection for burst traffic (peak inference) — request for a \"surge insurance\" add-on or guaranteed burst pool.

Also, procurement wants to understand any credits or short-term concessions you can offer while we migrate a new product line onto Redwood. Can you send a proposal with a few options (term/commit/price-hold/credits)?

Thanks,
Emma

Hi Emma — great to hear usage ramping, congrats on the traction. Attached is a short proposal with three options (summary below). I copied pricing and operations so we can move quickly.

Quick summary (see attached PDF for line items):
- Option A — 12mo price-hold: 30% commit increase, 12-month price hold at current effective rate, includes 8 weeks of free burst credits (one-time) to smooth migration.
- Option B — 24mo discount: 20% commit increase, 24-month price hold with 8% list discount and staggered true-up at year 2.
- Option C — Flexible commit + surge insurance add-on: smaller committed uplift (10%) + surge-insurance (monthly fee) that guarantees a burst pool with pre-warmed capacity and usage-based billing above commit.

We can also structure a limited credit for migration risk (portfolio credit applied over first 3 invoices) if that helps procurement.

Attachments: FastLedger_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal with revenue schedule).

Subject: FW: Renewal discussion: FastLedger — need guidance on concession appetite

Ben / Vanessa / Markus — forwarding FastLedger's request. Key asks: 30% commit increase, 12 mo price-hold; want surge capacity protection and short-term credits for migration.

My thinking:
- Baseline: agree to 12mo price-hold if commit increase >= 30% with 6% margin hit (target reduced by credits).
- Concession: offer 8 weeks burst credits (no charge) + optional surge-insurance (paid monthly).
- If they push on deeper discount, propose a limited sign-up credit (apply across 3 invoices) instead of lowering list price.

Can we do a one-time \"surge insurance\" pilot (free for 3 months) to remove the operational risk? That would be temporary and convertible to the paid add-on after pilot.

Please advise — need to give Emma an answer by EOD Fri so procurement can align with their internal timelines.

Thanks,
Tessa
